clonidine.text: Forum posters include clonidine in stress stacks, alongside pregnenolone and cyproheptadine, aiming for lower stress, calmer nights and a more rested look. It is a prescription blood-pressure and ADHD drug; its use for appearance is anecdotal and has not been tested.

zuranolone.text: Zuranolone is an approved postpartum depression drug that occasionally comes up in neurosteroid and mood-recovery discussions. Any appearance link runs through mood and sleep improvement; it has been studied for depression only, not for looks.

allopregnanolone.text: Allopregnanolone is a natural progesterone-derived neurosteroid discussed in stress and sleep circles for its calming action on the brain. Interest in looks is indirect, via stress and rest; it has been studied for postpartum depression and not for appearance.

kava-kavalactones.text: Users take kava to unwind, ease anxiety and sleep better, with the idea that lower stress shows in a more relaxed, rested face. Small trials have looked at anxiety, while appearance outcomes have not been studied.

lavender-oil-capsules-silexan.text: Silexan is taken as a calming supplement, and users in recovery-focused circles pair it with better sleep and lower stress for a more rested look. Placebo-controlled trials cover anxiety; appearance use is untested.

hops-extract.text: Hops extract is included in sleep blends, often with valerian or chamomile, by people seeking deeper sleep and a more rested appearance. Human evidence for its sedative effect is limited, and appearance use is unstudied.

chain: Claimed IGF-1 and BMP-2 bone signaling
propranolol.text: Forum posters take propranolol to calm physical anxiety symptoms before social situations, and some promote a theory that it stimulates bone growth and improves facial structure. The anxiety use is established medically; the bone-growth idea is untested in humans.

tianeptine.text: Tianeptine is an antidepressant that appears in gray-market stress and mood stacks, where users want less stress and more energy for daily life. Its link to looks is indirect via mood; it has been studied for depression, not appearance.

tiratricol-triac.text: Tiratricol was once sold as a fat-burner because thyroid-hormone analogues raise metabolic rate, which people link to leanness. It is approved today for a rare genetic disorder; its use for fat loss rests on case reports and anecdote rather than trials.

levothyroxine-t4.text: Some users aim to correct low-normal thyroid levels with levothyroxine to feel better, hold less water and fat, and look leaner. It is the standard treatment for hypothyroidism; appearance gains in people with normal thyroid function have not been studied.

desiccated-thyroid-armour.text: Desiccated thyroid is used by people who believe fuller T3 and T4 supply improves energy, metabolism and body composition. It is an older hypothyroidism treatment; its use as a slimming or appearance aid is based on anecdote and has not been trialled.

chain: Feminizing changes or reduced hair growth
medroxyprogesterone-acetate.text: Medroxyprogesterone acetate is used within feminizing hormone therapy and for hirsutism, where altered hormone signaling changes body shape and hair growth. These appearance uses are off-label to its contraceptive role, with limited trial data for them.

megestrol-acetate.text: Megestrol is a progestin appetite stimulant approved for cancer and AIDS wasting, and it comes up in forum talk about gaining weight on a thin frame. Weight gain is its documented effect in illness; cosmetic or physique use is untested.

cyproheptadine.text: Users take cyproheptadine to boost appetite and eat more while bulking or gaining weight, and some forum posts stack it with pregnenolone and clonidine for stress. Appetite gain is documented, mainly in children; cosmetic weight gain has not been studied.

methylphenidate.text: Appetite loss is a documented effect of methylphenidate, so some users take it to eat less and lean out, or to focus better. It is an ADHD stimulant; its use as a weight-loss aid has not been tested.

amphetamine-adderall.text: Forum posters use prescription stimulants to suppress appetite and lose weight, and some claim they improve social ease and gym performance. Appetite suppression is a documented side effect; weight loss and appearance outcomes were not the studied purpose.

lisdexamfetamine-vyvanse.text: Vyvanse is discussed for its appetite-reducing effect, and it is approved for binge-eating disorder as well as ADHD. Users interested in leaning out cite that effect; weight loss for appearance has not been the studied purpose.

quinine-skin-bleaching.text: Quinine appears in reports of unregulated skin-lightening products, where users sought a lighter complexion. It is an antimalarial and tonic-water flavoring; its lightening effect is a claim with no supporting research.

ascorbyl-glucoside.text: Ascorbyl glucoside is a stabilised vitamin C derivative used in serums to brighten skin, even tone and slow visible aging. Studies on vitamin C support these aims generally, while research on this specific derivative is small.

cetyl-tranexamate-mesylate.text: Cetyl tranexamate mesylate is placed in serums aimed at dark spots and uneven tone, as a topical form of tranexamic acid. Evidence consists of early cosmetic-grade data with little independent testing.

piroctone-olamine.text: Piroctone olamine is used in anti-dandruff shampoos to clear flakes and keep the scalp healthy so hair looks cleaner. It has been compared head-to-head with zinc pyrithione for dandruff; it is a scalp-health ingredient, not studied for hair growth.

zinc-pyrithione.text: Zinc pyrithione is the classic active in dandruff shampoos, used to clear flakes and calm seborrheic dermatitis for a cleaner-looking scalp and hair. It is well studied for dandruff; it is not promoted for hair growth.

selenium-disulfide.text: Selenium disulfide shampoos such as Selsun Blue are used to clear dandruff and scalp scaling for a cleaner look. It is studied for scalp conditions, and hair growth is not its documented use.

erythrulose.text: Erythrulose is a sugar used with DHA in self-tanners to give a sunless tan, a color change visible within hours. It tends to develop more slowly and fade more evenly in cosmetic-industry descriptions; independent trials were not found.

silymarin-milk-thistle.text: Silymarin is a milk thistle liver supplement that some users take for its antioxidant chemistry, hoping for clearer skin or slower visible aging. The skin and appearance role is theoretical and has not been tested.

vilon.text: Vilon is a Lys-Glu dipeptide from Khavinson's Russian peptide bioregulator program, discussed in longevity circles as an anti-aging candidate. Data come from mouse and cell studies; no human trials or appearance link is known.

pinealon.text: Pinealon is a short peptide marketed for brain and anti-aging use in nootropic and longevity communities, with a looks angle drawn via sleep and healthy aging. Evidence is cell and rat data plus small Russian-language human reports.

thymogen.text: Thymogen is an immunomodulator dipeptide from Russian peptide research, discussed in longevity circles for its immune and anti-aging claims. Evidence is mostly animal and cell data with thin human reports; no appearance use is documented.

bronchogen.text: Bronchogen is a short peptide from Khavinson's bioregulator program aimed at lung tissue, discussed in longevity circles as an organ-specific anti-aging peptide. Data are rat and cell studies only; no human trials and no appearance link.

cardiogen.text: Cardiogen is a short peptide from Khavinson's bioregulator program aimed at heart tissue, discussed in longevity circles as an anti-aging peptide. Data are sparse rat and cell studies with no human trials; no appearance link is known.
